summary: Configure priority routing and route-level quota separation to prevent synchronized refill 429s
description:
Issue summary: AtlasSearch reports periodic 429 throttles across multiple backend services after they introduced synchronized hourly backfill batches and a short-lived API key rotation. Impact: customer-facing search indexer jobs see intermittent failures (approx 5-12% of jobs) during the top-of-hour backfill window. The failures manifest as 429 responses from the Redwood API and automatic retries exacerbate the problem. They are on a Dedicated pool with several microservices sharing a small set of shared API keys via an internal gateway.

Observed: 429 spikes align tightly with the hourly worker heartbeat and an orchestrated key refresh that creates many concurrent short sessions. The customer is asking for a configuration recipe to isolate background/bulk workloads from low-latency interactive routes and guidance to avoid synchronized refill events that cause tenant-level soft-throttles.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Customer runs 120 worker processes across 6 hosts that each kick off a backfill job at HH:00 with identical start times.
2) All workers use the same short-lived API key (rotated every 90 minutes) proxied through the customer gateway.
3) Workers open multiplexed HTTP/2 connections and issue batched embedding requests and real-time chat calls in parallel.
4) At the top-of-hour, the gateway streams a key refresh and restarts connections for all workers, generating a concentrated token-refill pattern at our ingress.
5) The customer observes tenant-level 429s and sawtooth token-window patterns on their dashboards and ours.
logs: 2026-03-10T10:00:03Z ingress: tenant=atlas id=conn-7f2a drop=429 reason=token-window-exhausted tokens_left=0
2026-03-10T10:00:04Z rate-limiter: tenant=atlas refill_window=60s window_tokens=0 burst_credit=120 origin=edge-proxy-a
comments: 2026-03-10 - Aisha (Reporter): We started seeing this after enabling a synchronized hourly backfill. The errors only happen during the first 2 minutes of the hour and then traffic normalizes. Can you advise configuration changes we should make on our end and whether Redwood can prevent tenant-level bleed between background and interactive traffic?

2026-03-10 - Support (Marco): Thanks, we can help. Initial hypothesis: synchronized worker start + shared short-lived key + identical retry/backoff leads to token-window exhaustion and health-probe-like accounting. Can you share your gateway connection pattern (HTTP/1 vs HTTP/2) and whether you multiplex several logical clients over the same connection?

2026-03-10 - Customer (AtlasSearch SRE): We're using HTTP/2 multiplexing with keepalive and the gateway rotates keys every 90m. We do multiplex and also open new connections on rotation. We can try staggering but need best practice guidance to avoid throughput impact.

2026-03-11 - SRE (Olga Petrov): We've captured the refill heatmap and see a sharp token depletion at HH:00. Suggest isolating heavy background routes and giving them a separate route-level quota or separate API key to avoid tenant-level bucket depletion. Also recommend jittered start times and exponential backoff with randomized jitter on retries.

2026-03-12 - Support (Marco): Ran a quick sim with a mirrored traffic pattern on our staging harness; changes that eliminated the simultaneous key rotation (staggered rotation + per-route keys) removed the 429 spike. Please see investigation notes for exact config suggestions.
investigation_notes: Hypothesis: Tenant-level token accounting is being exhausted because multiple logical clients share a single token bucket; synchronized rotation and identical worker start times create an intra-tenant spike that moves the tenant into soft-throttle (429) mode until the next refill tick.

Telemetry: Ingress heatmap shows >90% of tenant tokens consumed within a 20s window around HH:00. Token-window size = 60s; burst credits consumed fully in the spike. Related metrics: rate_limiter.window_hits, tenant:buckets_used, ingress.active_connections.

Tests: Replayed customer pattern on a staging dedicated pool with 100 workers; introducing 5-15s jitter per worker eliminated the sawtooth pattern. Creating a dedicated background route with its own quota prevented interactive route 429s even with the same global tenant throughput.

Risk: For Dedicated customers, changing quota separation is safe but customers must ensure route weight and billing alignment. Short-lived key rotation without jitter will continue to concentrate connection restarts at ingress and can be mitigated client-side.
Related PR: github.com/redwood/inference/pull/8421 adds a diagnostic flag for per-route token accounting to our staging runtime. Linked INT ticket created to track product-side improvements.
resolution_notes: 1) Create two API keys: one for interactive low-latency routes and one for background bulk/backfill jobs. Configure the gateway to route background job traffic to the bulk key and interactive traffic to the interactive key.

2) On the Redwood Console, configure route-level isolation (create a low-latency route and a bulk route) and set separate quota windows: smaller window and higher priority for low-latency route, larger sustained window for bulk.
3) Stagger worker start times with randomized jitter (recommended 5-30s) and add client-side exponential backoff with randomized jitter for retries to avoid herd effects.
4) If using short-lived keys, make rotation asynchronous per-host (avoid global key swap at the same second).

- We enabled a temporary route-level shadow quota for atlas on staging to validate isolation. We will propose a permanent Console setting for quicker route split flows for Dedicated customers (product request raised).
- Added recommended runbook steps to Confluence: /confluence/runbooks/rate-limiter-adjustments (updated 2026-03-12).
- Customer to implement dual-key routing and staggered rotation and report back with a full-hour cycle results (assigned to AtlasSearch SRE).
- Internal: Product to consider a Dedicated UI flow for automated splitting of burst pools between interactive and bulk routes (linked INT-4210).

Outcome as of 2026-03-12: Atlas applied the two-key pattern and jittered starts in a controlled canary; they report reduction of 429 windows from ~90s to near-zero in the observed timeframe. Ticket remains open to confirm a full weekly run and to capture runbook edits before closing.
